No, the pedestrian will not prevail. Even if the adjuster knowingly misstated the law, misrepresentation requires justifiable reliance and resulting damages, and the pedestrian rejected the offer, hired an attorney, and won $550,000, so they neither relied on the statement nor were harmed by it. The team note's "special duty of trust" requirement isn't a general element of fraudulent misrepresentation, so I'm not relying on it. The claim fails on reliance and damages.

CONFIDENCE: 90
